identity_cases.note: Semantic-identity cases the projection must honor (spec §10.1). They are projection properties — the pair documents are not committed programs.
identity_cases.positional_operand_reversal: interval.sub(initial_clearance, length) vs interval.sub(length, initial_clearance): arguments are a sequence — the reversal computes [-199/2] vs [199/2] and must produce different semantic_sha256
identity_cases.declared_set_reorder: reordering methods, kind_products, requires, inputs, assumptions, premises, or requirements yields an identical semantic_sha256
identity_cases.annotation_named_identifiers: a proposition named note/label/description is a map key — preserved with its params; note@(geometry,scenario) vs note@(material,scenario) differ semantically, and an input or entity named likewise is preserved
identity_cases.annotation_at_declared_position: editing a method's label, a kind's gloss, or a source's statement changes document_sha256 only — semantic_sha256 identical
identity_cases.annotation_at_undeclared_position: a field named note/label/etc. where the schema declares none is malformed at admission — the projection never sees it
identity_cases.body_order: body is a sequence: reordering it is a different semantic document and, when it would admit a §4 forward reference, inadmissible before hashing

runtime_adversarial_rows.note: The remaining adversarial-matrix rows are execution/replay properties, exercised once EL-03/EL-04 exist; specified here so implementation cannot launder them into program semantics
runtime_adversarial_rows.transplanted_receipt: a receipt or output digest bound to a different invocation fails §7.O1 at digest comparison; the obligation stays open → not_evaluated
runtime_adversarial_rows.forged_certificate_recomputed_hashes: a certificate whose postcondition does not hold under the named check fails §7.O2; recomputing outer digests does not help (ADR-0026 context equality)
runtime_adversarial_rows.process_failure_or_absent_output: no observation → §7.O1 produces nothing → runtime obligation unmet → not_evaluated
runtime_adversarial_rows.budget_exhaustion: any §11 bound exceeded is an explicit bounded refusal, distinct from unsupported and from success
runtime_adversarial_rows.presentation_only_change: editing annotation fields or reordering declared-set arrays produces identical semantic identities and identical derivations; document digests may differ honestly (§10.1)
runtime_adversarial_rows.semantic_mutation: adding a requires entry, changing a kind, changing declared params, or reordering positional operands changes semantic_sha256 — a new library identity; existing contexts refuse it rather than reinterpret
runtime_adversarial_rows.method_library_lifecycle: lifecycle material is supplied per evaluation context (§10.2). Cases: withdrawn library entry + active method entry → method is not_evaluated.withdrawn (no override, all refusal reasons preserved); two same-key entries with different states → lifecycle_conflict refusal at bind; expired + withdrawn on one method → not_evaluated naming both reasons; no applicable entries → method.lifecycle premise records 'absent' — usable and visible, not an implicit active
runtime_adversarial_rows.requirement_limit_changed: the limit is a premise of the requirement rule; changing 1/4 to 7/20 or 9/20 re-derives the verdict while every method-application premise is preserved (the three clearance programs pin this)
runtime_adversarial_rows.input_geometry_method_or_material_change: dependency edges (§8.3) identify every affected application — including edges under projected relations; derivation diff explains the change semantically rather than as a hash delta
runtime_adversarial_rows.imported_derivation_dropped_assumption: replay compares the import's declared assumption set against the source record's propagated assumptions (§9); a dropped assumption is a mismatch on the import premise
